questions.prompt: Two Linux containers share one ACI container group. The app listens on port 8080; a helper listens on port 8081. Only port 8080 is exposed on the group public IP. Which endpoint lets the app call the helper using their shared local network?

options.explanation: Containers in one group share the local network; port 8081 identifies the helper listener.

options.text: The group public IP on port 8081
options.explanation: Port 8081 is not exposed on the public endpoint. The internal helper can instead be reached through localhost.
The local network is appropriate, but port 8080 is the app listener rather than the helper.

options.text: The image registry hostname on port 8081
options.explanation: The registry stores container images; it does not address the running helper.

questions.prompt: An ACI batch process returns exit code 0 on success and a nonzero code on failure. The configuration must explicitly request retry after failure and leave successful completion terminated. Which configuration expresses this policy while preserving the process outcome?

options.text: Restart policy OnFailure; pass through the process exit code unchanged.
options.explanation: OnFailure requests retries for nonzero exits and leaves exit-code-0 completion terminated.

options.text: Restart policy Always; pass through the process exit code unchanged.
options.explanation: Always also restarts successful termination, contrary to the requirement.

options.text: Restart policy Never; pass through the process exit code unchanged.
options.explanation: Never does not explicitly request failure retries. Documentation warns that platform restarts after nonzero exits can still occur; that caveat is not an explicit retry policy.

options.text: Restart policy OnFailure; wrap the command to return exit code 0 after every run.
options.explanation: Mapping failures to zero hides the failure outcome from OnFailure, so the policy does not receive the nonzero exit needed for a retry.

questions.prompt: A Linux ACI batch task writes result files through a mounted directory. The files must survive deletion of its container group. Which storage configuration meets the requirement?

options.text: Mount an Azure Files share for the results and retain the share after deleting the group.
options.explanation: The external share persists independently of the container group, preserving files written to the mount.

options.text: Write the results only to the container writable layer.
options.explanation: The local writable layer is not durable across deletion of the container group.

options.text: Mount an emptyDir volume for the results and delete the group after completion.
options.explanation: emptyDir can share files within the group, but its contents do not survive group deletion.

options.text: Mount an Azure Files share for the results and delete that share with the group.
options.explanation: The storage is external, but deleting the share removes the retained results the requirement needs.
